Prebuilt **Windows x86-64** binaries of `k3`, the pure-C Kimi K3 inference engine from
[FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c](https://github.com/FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c).

This is a packaging release. The engine is upstream **v1.1.0** plus one later upstream
fix (below), built for Windows without `-march=native`, so the binary runs on CPUs other
than the one that built it. `k3.exe --help` reports `1.1.0` because the version string
in the source didn't change.

## Downloads

| File | CPU requirement | Use when |
|---|---|---|
| `k3-1.1.0-windows-x64-avx2.zip` | AVX2 + FMA: Intel Haswell (2013) or newer, any AMD Ryzen | **Default. Pick this one.** |
| `k3-1.1.0-windows-x64-generic.zip` | Any 64-bit x86 CPU | Only if the avx2 build exits with `0xC000001D` (illegal instruction). Uses the scalar kernels, so it's slower. |
| `SHA256SUMS.txt` | | Checksums for both zips |

Each zip contains `k3.exe`, `LICENSE`, `NOTICE` and `WINDOWS.txt`.

- **No installer, no DLLs.** It's statically linked and imports only `KERNEL32.dll` and
  `msvcrt.dll`, which ship with every version of Windows.
- **Verify the download** in PowerShell:
  `Get-FileHash .\k3-1.1.0-windows-x64-avx2.zip -Algorithm SHA256`, then compare the
  result with `SHA256SUMS.txt`.
- **Quick check:** `.\k3.exe --help` and `.\k3.exe --list-presets`.

## You still need the model

This release contains the engine only. To run inference you need the Kimi K3 checkpoint,
which is about 1.56 TB and downloaded separately. See the README's *Quick start* and
[docs/QUICKSTART.md](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.1.0-win.1/docs/QUICKSTART.md).
On Windows, pass non-ASCII prompts with `--prompt-file`, because Windows re-encodes argv
to the active code page.

## What's in the engine

Everything in upstream
[v1.1.0](https://github.com/FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#110---2026-10-02):
`--chat` with K3's chat format, `--preset ultra` / `--ultra-low-memory` (the full model in
an 8 GB memory budget), `--trunk-ring`, safe Ctrl-C, `--threads`, and hardened checkpoint
parsing.

Also included, from after v1.1.0:

- **fix(trunk):** a prefetched layer is now charged as a read to the bind that reaches it,
  so the trunk report's hit and read counts no longer depend on thread timing. This changes
  counting only; the model's output is unchanged
  ([`7721a1b`](https://github.com/FareedKhan-dev/kimi-k3-in-c/commit/7721a1b)).

## How it was built and verified

- Built with MSYS2 MinGW-w64 GCC on GitHub's `windows-latest` runner (`-O3 -fopenmp`,
  `-static`) by [`windows-release.yml`](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.1.0-win.1/.github/workflows/windows-release.yml).
  To reproduce it, run `scripts/build-windows.sh`.
- The same job ran the full weightless test suite on Windows with the avx2 flags shipped
  here: `22 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped`, `VERDICT: ENGINE MATCHES THE REFERENCE EXACTLY`.
- **Not verified:** inference on real Kimi K3 weights on Windows, because CI doesn't have
  the checkpoint. Tokenizer parity didn't run either, since it needs the checkpoint's
  `tiktoken.model`, which upstream CI also lacks.

Build instructions: [docs/BUILD-WINDOWS.md](https://github.com/s81/kimi-work-8Gb/blob/v1.1.0-win.1/docs/BUILD-WINDOWS.md).
